hypothesis: On the complete LongMemEval-S raw-session candidate set, Pareto Top-K has higher macro session-level Recall@5 than the fixed weighted scalar baseline when both methods receive identical lexical-relevance proxy, retention, and importance features.

data.candidate_identity: candidate entries are keyed by list position and aligned across haystack_session_ids, haystack_sessions, and haystack_dates; retain repeated non-qrel IDs as separate dated candidates; each qrel ID must map to exactly one candidate position per question
data.split: none; all question/session-overlap component; exploratory descriptive evaluation only

lexical_relevance_proxy.name: BM25 raw-session lexical score
lexical_relevance_proxy.tokenizer: lowercase ASCII alphanumeric tokens via regex [a-z0-9]+; all conversation message contents concatenated; no stopword filtering; distinct query terms
lexical_relevance_proxy.idf: ln((N - df + 0.5) / (df + 0.5)); term score includes Lucene's (k1+1) multiplier

retention.equation: exp(-lambda0 * max(0, question_date - session_date)_days / (1 + eta * ln(1 + access_count)))
retention.timestamp_rule: as_of cutoff time is question_date; future-dated sessions have zero age in the full-haystack primary analysis

importance.reason: LongMemEval has no importance feature; use the Java MemoryNode primitive double default and do not infer labels

candidate_features.graph_relevance: omitted; the selected production analogue is the three-objective MemoryNode route

pareto.selection: non-dominated fronts; normalized crowding distance with objective-boundary infinity; descending lexical relevance tie-break; stable input order thereafter

weighted_sum_baseline.source: MemoryScoringServiceImpl.computeCompositeScore production constants; importance=0 means the activation floor does not apply
weighted_sum_baseline.selection: descending score; stable input order for exact ties

primary_analysis.candidate_universe: all haystack sessions provided for each question; original answer_session_ids retained
primary_analysis.stratification: question_type descriptive aggregates; no hypothesis tests
primary_analysis.inference: descriptive paired deltas only; no p-values, confidence intervals, or independent-question claims

sensitivity_analysis.qrels: do not change or filter the original answer_session_ids; unavailable qrels count as misses
sensitivity_analysis.purpose: expose temporal-cutoff sensitivity; not the primary benchmark setting

leakage_controls: Answers and qrels are accessed only by the final metric aggregation, never by candidate features or rank computation.

No query split, parameter tuning, or qrel modification is performed; the scoring implementation was corrected before the frozen analysis was accepted and the preliminary run is retained only as invalidated diagnostic output.
All candidates for a question are shared exactly between the two ranking methods; repeated non-qrel candidate IDs are retained by position and not deduplicated.
Question/session overlap counts each session ID once per question; each qrel ID must map to exactly one candidate position, and metric hits are unique by session ID.
The complete LongMemEval-S set is one connected component under shared candidate session IDs; question-level significance tests are prohibited.

resources.execution: local CPU, Python standard library only
